_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-07 · SkyMiner — both of Sam's decisions are shipped and live. The feedback queue turned out to be 53% our own test robot, and it had already reported three of the last four fixes weeks early.
_status: Two questions were waiting for Sam and he answered both, so both are now live on Sierra (deploy 11). First: when someone asks about a certificate their college hasn't set up yet, Sierra used to go quiet to avoid looking like she was poaching students off a college's own web page. She no longer does. The new line is that she never HIDES anything that changes your outcome — she'll tell you where the credit exists today and that your college could adopt it — but she never SELLS you on going elsewhere. Second: when your college doesn't offer it, she now gives all three parts of the answer instead of stopping after two: your own college first, then the colleges that have already set this up (proof it works), then the nearest colleges that actually teach the subject — even if none of them has set up the credit yet. That last part is the one that had gone missing, and it's the only part that gives someone somewhere to go this month. Separately, opening the feedback inbox produced an uncomfortable finding: of 53 ratings, 28 were written by our own automated test, every one of them a thumbs-down, so the headline said 38 complaints when only 10 were real. Worse, the real ones had already told us what to fix — a reviewer described the student-portal problem on 17 July, three weeks before it came up in conversation and got fixed. The test rows are now filtered out of the queue and the counts, and four reports whose fixes have shipped are marked done.

items.text: 📬 SEVEN FEEDBACK REPORTS STILL NEED YOU — the inbox is cleaned up (our test robot's 31 rows are filtered out of the queue and the counts, and 4 reports whose fixes have shipped are marked done). The most useful of what's left: someone asked how many colleges have a CPL counsellor listed and Sierra couldn't answer, though she names them one at a time — that's a build, not a bug. Two are data gaps you already know about (student counts per certificate). The rest need an eye: Modesto showing 75 early-childhood credit recommendations when its landing page shows 4; Sierra reading the Fullerton catalogue in one answer and not the next; a bare thumbs-down on College of the Canyons; and the 17 July 'I don't have a college yet' report, which the student-portal work probably fixed but nobody has confirmed. ⚠ Please don't invite the MAP and CO teams until this has an owner — it's now CA-06 on the ⚖️ Governance tab, and that tab will show you the untriaged count live.

🔗 STILL UNCHECKED: THE LINK SIERRA GIVES STUDENTS — creditforbeingyou.org/main/student. I can't reach that domain from here, so it has never been confirmed and it's now in front of every student who asks. One click tells us; it's a one-line fix if it's wrong.

🔍 FINISH THE POACHING AUDIT — now that the 'never hide facts, never sell' line is live, re-run the five-part review (Sierra's rule text, her per-audience voices, the context builders, the live guidance rows in the 🧭 pane, and the sibling report generators) to confirm nothing else still tells her to stay quiet. SkyHero's audit was still running when that session ended and was never reported.

📚 REFRESH SIERRA'S EXHIBIT LIST — unchanged and still the biggest limit. Her copy covers 2,397 exhibits across 59 colleges; MAP has 123, and her college profiles were last refreshed 25 June. American River, LA Mission and West LA all give CPR credit and she cannot see them. Touches a shared table production reads, so walk Sam through the impact first.

🔢 WIRE MALONE'S STUDENT×CREDIT-RECOMMENDATION VIEW into the funding backlog builder once the view name lands. The 11.8MB export could not be read directly (the Drive connector caps at 10MB). Agreed columns are the 8 non-identifying ones; Sam wants small-group suppression at fewer than 10.

🔍 SIERRA STILL STOPS ONE STEP SHORT — you chose that when someone's own college doesn't offer a certificate, she should give three things: your college first, then who's already set it up, then the nearest colleges that actually TEACH it. The first two now work live. The third doesn't yet — asked about carpentry at LA Harbor she names Norco and Santiago Canyon (who award the credit, ~50 miles away) but not Rio Hondo or LA Trade Tech, which teach carpentry right there. We know that data exists because she lists exactly those colleges when asked the same question a different way. I've left it measured rather than guessed at — nothing to do on your side, just so you know it's half-landed.

🧪 FIND OUT WHY SIERRA SKIPS THE NEAREST TEACHING COLLEGE — measure before touching prompt text. Either the course-catalog search returns a thin list when the question names a college (mode 7's wording includes 'Los Angeles Harbor College'; the working question doesn't), or the list is there and she just doesn't use it. Those need opposite fixes and guessing between them is how this workstream has burned weeks before. Extend tests/sierra_geo_ranking.test.js to assert the ordered college list for this exact query.

⚖️ THREE NEW GOVERNANCE ROWS TO ASSIGN — you were right that neither the test invitation nor Sierra generally was on the register. Added: DR-11 (who decides what Sierra tells the public — in practice that's been you personally, four times in two days), CA-06 (Sierra feedback triage, which shows its own untriaged count live), and OQ-07 (what has to be true before we invite the MAP and CO teams). All three need an owner, same as every other row.
